task_description: The script computes general and descriptive statistics for vector or raster layers in QGIS, including total count, null count, mean, standard deviation, variance, skewness, min, max, median, and quartiles (25%, 75%). It dynamically adapts to layer type (vector/raster), selects appropriate fields or bands, applies user-specified decimal precision, and populates a UI form with results. Outputs are displayed in QLineEdit widgets (e.g., mean, std dev, quantiles) and not exported as files or layers.

The script tests QGIS Processing algorithms that download OpenStreetMap (OSM) data via the Overpass API for specific geographic queries (raw, spatial area, 'in', 'around', and extent-based), returning vector layers split by geometry type (points, lines, multiline strings, multipolygons) representing OSM elements matching the query criteria (e.g., amenity=bench). Each test mocks HTTP responses to validate correct algorithm behavior, input parameter handling (e.g., timeout, server URL, CRS-aware extent reprojection), and output layer instantiation.

task_name: Count vehicle trajectories at traffic gates
task_description: The script tests the 'export_to_json' algorithm of the Traffic Trajectory Toolkit (TTT) in QGIS Processing. It first runs 'count_trajectories_gate' to compute per-gate traffic metrics (vehicle count, average speed, average acceleration) from point-based trajectory data and line-based gate geometries, then exports the resulting gate-layer attributes—including channel, traveler class, time interval bounds, vehicle_count, speed_avg, acceleration_avg—into a JSON array with one object per gate. The test validates that exactly 3 gates are exported, each with 7 specific fields and correct keys.

The script tests the behavior of a QGIS plugin ('AppendFeaturesToLayer') when updating spatial target layers using non-spatial source layers (e.g., database tables without geometry). It verifies that attribute updates occur correctly for matching features (by key field 'name'), appended features receive NULL geometries, and existing geometries in the target layer remain completely unchanged — confirming geometry preservation during attribute-only updates.

The script performs spatial arithmetic operations (difference, sum, maximum) on user-selected GIS vector layers representing atmospheric deposition (e.g., NH3, NOX), validating input layers for mandatory fields ('fid', 'dep_NH3', 'dep_NOX'). It executes QGIS Processing algorithms ('imaer:relate_difference', 'imaer:relate_sum', 'imaer:relate_maximum') to generate a new output vector layer with computed deposition values, applies IMAER-specific styling, and adds the result to the QGIS project. The workflow is interactive via a dialog with configurable layer inputs and operation type selection.

The script extracts outlet points along a stream network by interpolating points near the downstream ends of stream lines (using a dynamic distance based on line length), rasterizes the stream network using a DEM as base, and then snaps the interpolated points to the nearest stream pixel within a 40-unit distance using the Jenson Snap Pour Points algorithm. The output is a vector point layer of snapped outlets.

The script interpolates elevation values from a digital elevation model (DEM) raster layer onto a pixel-center-aligned vector grid, then reprojects the grid and generates a new raster using TIN interpolation with linear method. The output is a resampled elevation raster at a specified pixel size, aligned to the input extent and CRS.

The script places master contour line labels for Brazilian topographic mapping by identifying contour lines whose elevation values are multiples of a scale-dependent index (e.g., 50 m at 1:25,000), extracting QGIS-rendered label bounding polygons from map layers within geographic boundaries, clipping master contours against those label polygons, splitting and buffering interpolated midpoints to isolate candidate label placement segments, and populating a dedicated symbol layer (edicao_simb_cota_mestra_l) with geometry and elevation values while clearing the 'texto_edicao' attribute on original contour lines. Outputs include updated contour layer attributes and new features in the contour symbol layer.
